intro_html:
Some dinners try to be fancy. This one just tries to be good, and it lands. Italian Chicken Tortellini Skillet is chicken, cheese tortellini, and a tomato cream sauce that tastes like it simmered all afternoon when it really came together in about half an hour. One pan, real food, and a plate that feels like a restaurant charged you eighteen dollars for it.

Here is the honest pitch. Every serving carries 37 grams of protein at 535 calories, and the whole thing cooks in a single skillet from start to finish in 30 minutes. That is the math I like: big flavor, tidy cleanup, and numbers that make sense.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3 lb, cut into 1/2-inch pieces (about 7 breasts) (1400 g)
Dried Basil (Great Value): 1 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon (4 g)
Dried Oregano (Great Value): 1 tablespoon plus 1/2 teaspoon (4 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): a scant 1/2 teaspoon (1 g)
Diced Tomatoes (Great Value): 6 cups with their juice (about three and a half 14 oz cans) (1438 g)
Cheese Tortellini (Great Value): 2 lb 11 oz (about 10 1/2 cups) (1225 g)

Batch total: about $27.46 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.96 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $37.39 across 14 servings, roughly $2.67 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $9.49 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $46.88. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html:
Here is where it gets good. Spread across all 14 servings, this comes out to ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a tortellini and cream dinner, the kind a restaurant lists in the double digits, for pocket change per box.

Run that math over a week of lunches and the savings stack up fast. Add our one dollar a month membership for the full board of recipes priced to the penny, and you can eat like this every week without wondering where the paycheck went.
shop_smart:
Buy the chicken smart. This batch wants 3 pounds of boneless skinless breast, about 7 of them, so reach for a family pack instead of the little foam trays. You get exactly what the recipe cuts into half inch pieces, and the bigger pack usually treats your wallet better per pound.

The tortellini does the heavy lifting, and you need a real pile of it, 2 pounds 11 ounces, or roughly 10 and a half cups. Fresh or frozen both work here, so buy whichever is priced better the day you shop. Frozen usually wins and it keeps until you are ready to cook.

Do not overthink the pantry. Dried basil, oregano, thyme, salt, and a scant half teaspoon of red pepper flakes are staples most of us already own, and this uses about a tablespoon each of the basil, oregano, and salt, so a jar you have on hand likely covers it with room left. Roasted red peppers come in a jar, and 1 and 3 quarter cups chopped is most of a standard one. For the tomatoes, grab the 14 ounce cans, you need about three and a half of them for the 6 cups of diced tomatoes with their juice.
make_it:
Heat the oil in a large skillet or saucepan over medium. Add the chicken, cut into half inch pieces, and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring as needed, until it is no longer pink. At 3 pounds you may want to sear in two rounds so the pan browns the meat instead of steaming it.

Add the garlic, dried basil, oregano, salt, thyme, and red pepper flakes. Cook one minute, just until the kitchen smells like an Italian place. Now stir in the diced tomatoes with their juice, the chopped roasted red peppers, and the heavy cream.

In a small bowl, whisk the chicken broth and cornstarch together until smooth, then stir it into the pan. That is your thickener, so do not skip the whisk or you invite lumps.

Add the tortellini, bring it up to medium high until it simmers, then drop to medium low, cover, and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the pasta is tender. Stir in the chopped spinach, mozzarella, and Parmesan until the cheese melts into the sauce. Taste, then serve.
portion_html:
This batch fills 14 containers, and fair portions come from the scale, not the eyeball. Weigh the full pot, tare off the pot weight, and divide what is left by 14. That gives you a gram target per box so nobody gets shorted the chicken and nobody ends up with a lonely scoop of sauce.

Ladle it warm, tortellini and sauce together, and each container lands at 535 calories with 37 grams of protein. Cool it down, seal it up, and it reheats like it was made that morning.

upsell_html: Make it once and it earns a permanent spot in the rotation. Big protein, real comfort, one pan to wash. Cook a batch this Sunday, line up your 14 containers, and let future you thank present you every time lunch rolls around.
